items.question: In what forms does Śiva abide within the act of worship?
premises: Worship involves a worshipper, worship, and an object of worship.
All these elements are present in the act.
Śiva abides as all these elements.
items.inference: Śiva is the worshipper, the worship, and the worshipped.
items.plain_english: The worshipper, the worship, and the worshipped—all this stands as Śiva.

items.question: How does worship occur for one who recognizes Śiva in all forms?
premises: All forms are manifestations of Śiva.
Enjoyment engages with these forms.
Such engagement constitutes worship for the speaker.
items.inference: For one established in Śiva, enjoyment of all forms is worship.
items.plain_english: In all forms, my worship takes place through enjoyment.

items.question: What is the goal, agent, and means when one moves toward Śiva?
premises: The goal of movement is Śiva.
The one who moves is Śiva.
The means of movement is Śiva.
items.inference: In approaching Śiva, the goal, agent, and means are all Śiva.
items.plain_english: I go to Śiva, I go as Śiva, with Śiva as my means.

items.question: Who is the enjoyer and what is enjoyed in the state of Śiva?
premises: Śiva is the enjoyer.
Śiva is the object of enjoyment.
The means of enjoyment among Śivas is Śiva.
items.inference: Enjoyer, enjoyed, and means of enjoyment are all Śiva.
items.plain_english: Śiva is the enjoyer, Śiva is the enjoyed, and among Śivas the means is Śiva.

items.question: How are doer, action, and instrument unified in Śiva?
premises: Śiva is the doer.
Śiva is the action.
The speaker is Śiva of the nature of the instrument.
items.inference: Doer, action, and instrument are all identical with Śiva.
items.plain_english: Śiva is the doer, Śiva is the action, and I am Śiva, of the nature of the instrument.

rows.grounds: by meditation and by refraining from action

items.question: What need is there for contemplation or non-doing if Śiva is ever manifest?
premises: Śiva is ever shining forth.
Contemplation and non-doing are means to realization.
What is always present does not require such means.
items.inference: For the ever-manifest Śiva, contemplation and non-doing are unnecessary.
items.plain_english: What need is there for contemplation or non-doing, since Śiva is ever shining forth?

items.question: Which sensory objects are included in the totality identified with Śiva?
premises: Objects of sight are included.
Objects of touch, smell, and taste are included.
All such sensory objects are being enumerated.
items.inference: All objects of the senses fall within the scope of Śiva-nature.
items.plain_english: Whatever is to be seen, whatever is to be touched, whatever is to be smelled, and whatever is to be tasted—

rows.grounds: in what is to be approached
in what is to be taken
in what is to be expressed

items.question: What further domains of experience are always included in Śiva-nature?
premises: What is to be reached, grasped, and spoken is included.
Pleasure and other states are included.
This inclusion holds at all times.
items.inference: All domains of action and feeling are always pervaded by Śiva.
items.plain_english: In what is to be reached, grasped, and spoken, and likewise in pleasure and so on, always—

rows.grounds: in what is to be considered
in what is to be esteemed
in what is to be understood

items.question: How does steadfast connection relate to cognition of all things as Śiva?
premises: What is to be thought, regarded, and known is included.
Steadfast connection supports this recognition.
All cognitive objects are encompassed.
items.inference: Through steadfast connection, all objects of cognition are recognized as Śiva.
uncertainties: abhimātavye: precise nuance of 'regarded/esteemed' in this context
items.plain_english: In what is to be thought, regarded, and known, through steadfast connection—

items.question: What conclusion is established about the nature of all enumerated things?
premises: All previously enumerated domains have been presented.
These domains constitute the whole of experience.
They are established as having Śiva as their essence.
items.inference: All that has been enumerated is of the nature of Śiva.
items.plain_english: All this, to this extent, has been established as being of the nature of Śiva.

items.question: What transformation occurs in the self when all is recognized as Śiva?
premises: All things are of the nature of Śiva.
This recognition can pervade every aspect.
The self becomes identified with that nature.
items.inference: Every self becomes wholly pervaded by Śiva in every way.
items.plain_english: The self of everyone becomes wholly consisting of Śiva, in every way.

rows.grounds: in the hollow of the mouth

items.question: Where and upon whom is the act of grace performed in this lineage?
premises: The sages are recipients of grace.
Grace is enacted in their mouths.
This act occurs among those very sages.
items.inference: The act of grace is performed in the mouths of those sages.
uncertainties: vaktra+kuhare: may imply inspired speech or direct transmission
items.plain_english: The act of grace took place in the mouths of those sages.

items.question: What condition of the teaching prompted a new act of grace?
premises: The teaching existed in places like Kalāpigrāma.
That teaching had ceased.
This cessation created a need for intervention.
items.inference: The cessation of the teaching in places like Kalāpigrāma set the stage for grace.
items.plain_english: When the teaching had ceased in Kalāpigrāma and other places—

rows.grounds: for the sake of bestowing grace
on the surface of the earth

items.question: Why did a divine figure descend and urge action on earth?
premises: The teaching had ceased.
A figure descended for the sake of grace.
This figure urged action on earth.
items.inference: A descent occurred on earth to restore the teaching through grace.
uncertainties: avatīrṇaḥ: subject implied from context, likely Śiva or a sage
items.plain_english: He descended on earth for the sake of grace and urged action.

items.question: What instruction was given to preserve the esoteric teaching?
premises: The scripture must not be cut off.
The teaching is secret.
An arrangement must be made to preserve it.
items.inference: The command was to preserve the secret scripture so it would not perish.
items.plain_english: Make it such that the secret scripture may not be cut off.

items.question: How was the lineage continued to preserve the secret teaching?
premises: A means was needed to preserve the teaching.
A mind-born son was created.
This son was named Tryambakāditya.
items.inference: The lineage was continued through the creation of a mind-born son named Tryambakāditya.
items.plain_english: He created a mind-born son named Tryambakāditya.

items.question: What did Tryambakāditya do after being created to continue the lineage?
premises: Tryambakāditya was created as a mind-born son.
He went to a cave named Tryambaka.
This action followed his creation.
items.inference: Tryambakāditya went to the Tryambaka cave as part of his spiritual mission.
items.plain_english: He too, having gone properly to the cave named Tryambaka, thereafter—

items.question: What attainment did Tryambakāditya and his son achieve in the lineage?
premises: Tryambakāditya became accomplished.
He leapt up into the sky.
His son likewise achieved the same.
items.inference: Both Tryambakāditya and his son attained perfection and ascended.
uncertainties: kham utpapāta: may indicate yogic ascent or passing away
items.plain_english: Being accomplished, he leapt up into the sky; his son also did likewise, likewise.

items.question: How long did the lineage of accomplished sons continue in this account?
premises: The lineage continued through successive sons.
This continued up to the fifteenth son.
Each was skilled in all scriptures.
items.inference: The lineage of scripture-skilled sons continued until the fifteenth generation.
items.plain_english: This continued until the fifteenth son, who was skilled in all the scriptures.

rows.grounds: a woman of the brahmin class

items.question: What change in orientation marked the fifteenth descendant in the lineage?
premises: The fifteenth son was outward-facing.
A certain brahmin woman appears in the narrative.
This marks a shift in the lineage's course.
items.inference: The fifteenth descendant became outward-facing, leading to a new development involving a brahmin woman.
uncertainties: bahirmukhasya: may imply worldly orientation or loss of inward focus
items.plain_english: Then, for that outward-facing one, there was a certain brahmin woman.

items.question: Why did the outward-facing descendant seek the brahmin woman's daughter?
premises: He saw the daughter.
She was endowed with auspicious marks.
She was suitable for him.
items.inference: He sought the daughter because she was suitable and auspiciously marked.
items.plain_english: Having seen her daughter, endowed with auspicious marks and suitable for himself—

items.question: How did the descendant obtain the suitable daughter for himself?
premises: He found the daughter suitable.
He requested her from the brahmin woman.
He brought her with effort.
items.inference: Through request and effort, he brought the daughter to himself.
items.plain_english: Having requested her from that brahmin woman, he brought her with effort.

items.question: How did the lineage come to be established in Kashmir?
premises: A descendant was born from that union.
In time he wandered.
He arrived in Kashmir.
items.inference: Through wandering, a descendant of the lineage came to Kashmir.
uncertainties: yaḥ sa ca: correlative construction, referent is the son born of the union
items.plain_english: And in time, he who was born of him came wandering into Kashmir.

items.question: Who was born in Kashmir as a continuation of this lineage?
premises: The descendant arrived in Kashmir.
A son was born to him.
That son was the venerable Aruṇāditya.
items.inference: The lineage in Kashmir continued with the birth of the venerable Aruṇāditya.
items.plain_english: To him also was born the venerable one named Aruṇāditya.
